meals.name: The Folate Legend
meals.punLine: Vegemite and smashed avo on hot toast, which is about as Australian as a B-vitamin hit gets.
steps: Toast the bread and butter it while it is still hot.
Spread the Vegemite thinly, the way the nation intended.
Smash the avocado with a squeeze of lemon and pile it on top.
Finish with cracked pepper and eat it straight away.

meals.name: Hard Yolker
meals.punLine: A properly hard-boiled egg with a row of toast soldiers, because a firm yolk is the whole trick.
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook them for a full 8 minutes.
Cool them under cold water, then peel.
Halve one and check the yolk is firm all the way through, with no runny centre.
Cut hot buttered toast into soldiers and dunk away.

meals.name: Grate Expectations
meals.punLine: Cheddar cubes, crunchy Vita-Weats and cherry toms: hard cheese is far too dry for listeria to throw a party in.
steps: Cube the cheddar into fat little bricks.
Wash the cherry tomatoes well under running water and halve them.
Line everything up on a plate with the crackers.
Build each bite as you go so the crackers stay crunchy.

meals.name: Berry Nice
meals.punLine: Yoghurt, washed berries and a lazy drizzle of honey, and yes, honey is a green light for mum.
steps: Wash the berries well under running water and slice the big ones.
Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl or a tall glass.
Top with the berries and a scatter of oats.
Drizzle honey over the lot and eat it cold.

meals.name: Smooth Operator
meals.punLine: Banana, oats and milk in your own blender, so you are the juice bar and the hygiene inspector.
steps: Peel the banana and drop it into a clean blender.
Add the oats, cold milk, a little honey and a pinch of cinnamon.
Blend until it is smooth and thick.
Drink it fresh rather than parking it in the fridge for later.

meals.name: Date Night
meals.punLine: Medjool dates stuffed with peanut butter: nature's caramel, and peanuts in pregnancy are absolutely fine.
steps: Split each date down one side and lift the stone out.
Spoon peanut butter into the gap.
Press the date shut and roll it in crushed peanuts and a little salt.
Chill them for ten minutes if you like them firm.

meals.name: Trail Blazer
meals.punLine: A jar of nuts, seeds and dried fruit that lives in your bag for hunger that turns up with no warning.
steps: Tip everything into a big jar in roughly equal handfuls.
Shake it until the dried fruit stops clumping.
Portion some into a small container for your bag.
Keep the jar sealed and out of the sun.

meals.name: Pop Star
meals.punLine: Popcorn is a fully green, fibre-carrying snack that takes about four minutes flat.
steps: Heat a splash of oil in a big pot with a lid on.
Add the corn, cover it, and shake the pot as it pops.
Take it off the heat once the popping slows to a crawl.
Salt it, add parmesan if you are feeling fancy, and dive in.

meals.name: Chick Magnet
meals.punLine: Canned chickpeas roasted until they rattle: the salty crunch of chips, with a lot more iron.
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then dry them properly on a clean tea towel.
Toss them with oil, paprika and salt.
Roast at 200 degrees Celsius for about 30 minutes, until they rattle in the tray.
Let them cool for five minutes so they crisp up, then eat them warm.

meals.name: Nice Nice Baby
meals.punLine: Frozen banana blitzed to soft-serve texture at home, which is the version of soft serve that is on the menu.
steps: Peel and slice the bananas, then freeze them on a tray overnight.
Blitz the frozen slices with a splash of milk until they turn glossy and thick.
Swirl through peanut butter or cocoa if you want it fancy.
Serve it straight from your own blender, since this one waits for nobody.

meals.name: Corn To Be Wild
meals.punLine: Corn thins, cottage cheese and tomato: the crunchy, salty answer to a 3pm slump.
steps: Wash the tomato and slice it thinly.
Spread cottage cheese over the corn thins.
Top with the tomato, chives and plenty of pepper.
Keep the tub in the fridge and finish it within two days of opening.

meals.name: White Bean Dream
meals.punLine: The dip that stepped up while hummus is benched, and it does the job without a drop of tahini.
steps: Drain and rinse the beans well.
Blitz them with garlic, lemon juice, olive oil and salt until silky.
Leave the tahini out completely, since raw sesame is the part that is off the menu for now.
Wash and cut the veg sticks yourself, then dunk with purpose.

meals.name: The Legal Parmy
meals.punLine: Pub royalty, made legal: the chicken cooks right through and the ham grills steaming hot under the cheese.
steps: Crumb the chicken through beaten egg and panko, then bake or shallow fry it until it is cooked right through with no pink.
Spoon over the passata, lay the ham on top and cover it with mozzarella.
Grill until the cheese bubbles and the ham underneath is steaming hot: that heat is exactly what makes the ham safe.
Serve it immediately with hot chips and a salad you washed at home.

meals.name: Iron Man Bol
meals.punLine: A big bowl of bolognese pulling double duty as comfort food and an iron delivery system.
steps: Brown the mince with the onion, garlic and grated carrot until no pink is left.
Add the canned tomatoes and simmer gently for at least 30 minutes.
Boil the spaghetti and toss it through the sauce while both are hot.
Shower it with parmesan, and cool any leftovers fast, then reheat them once until steaming.

meals.name: Omega Bake
meals.punLine: Baked salmon and greens, delivering the omega-3 that fish is genuinely encouraged for.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius and rub the salmon with oil, salt and lemon.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the flesh is opaque and flakes all the way through.
Steam the greens and roast the baby potatoes alongside it.
Plate it hot, and count it as one of your 1 to 3 fish serves for the week.

meals.name: Wok This Way
meals.punLine: A fast chicken and veg stir-fry where everything, sprouts included, gets properly hot in the wok.
steps: Slice the chicken and stir-fry it over high heat until it is cooked right through.
Add the hard veg, garlic and ginger and keep everything moving.
Add the bean sprouts early rather than at the end, and cook them right through until they are hot and floppy: raw or barely warmed sprouts are the risky bit.
Splash in the soy sauce and serve it over hot rice straight from the wok.

meals.name: Spud Life
meals.punLine: A baked potato is a plate, a hug and a blank canvas all at once.
steps: Scrub the potatoes, prick them and bake at 200 degrees Celsius for about an hour, until they give when squeezed.
Split them open and fork butter through the fluffy middle.
Mix the canned tuna with corn and mayonnaise from a jar, not the house-made kind.
Pile it in, top with cheese and spring onion, and eat it while it is still steaming.

meals.name: Fried Rice, Done Nice
meals.punLine: Fried rice made fresh and served steaming, with the egg cooked firm and no second lap through the microwave.
steps: Cook the rice, cool it quickly and keep it in the fridge for no longer than a day.
Scramble the eggs in the hot wok until they are firmly set, then lift them out.
Fry the carrot and the frozen veg until they are hot right through.
Add the rice and toss until the whole lot is steaming, stir the egg back in, and serve it without reheating it again.

meals.name: Well-Done Wonder
meals.punLine: Homemade burgers cooked all the way through, so nobody has to ask how you want it done.
steps: Season the mince and shape it into patties.
Cook them 4 to 5 minutes a side, until the juices run clear and there is no pink in the middle.
Melt the cheese over the patties in the last minute and toast the buns in the pan.
Build with washed lettuce, sliced tomato and mayonnaise from a jar.

meals.name: Curry On
meals.punLine: A mild chickpea and veg curry that freezes beautifully and asks almost nothing of you.
steps: Soften the onion, garlic and ginger, then toast the curry powder for a minute.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk and drained chickpeas, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Wash the spinach and stir it through until it wilts.
Serve it hot over fresh rice, and freeze the extra in single portions.

meals.name: The Toastie Loophole
meals.punLine: Deli ham's redemption arc: steaming hot counts as cooked.
steps: Butter the outsides of two slices of bread.
Stack the ham and cheese in the middle.
Toast it until the cheese surrenders and the ham is steaming hot right through, because that heat is the entire loophole.
Give it a minute to stop being lava, then eat.

meals.name: Cooked-Roll Sushi Night
meals.punLine: Sushi night at your place, where every filling is cooked, canned or crunchy and nothing is raw.
steps: Cook the rice, season it with vinegar and let it cool to room temperature.
Cook the chicken right through in teriyaki sauce, then slice it.
Mix the canned tuna with jar mayonnaise, and slice the avocado and cucumber.
Roll, slice and eat straight away, keeping every filling cooked or canned rather than raw or smoked.

meals.name: Frittata Fiesta
meals.punLine: A veggie frittata set firm right to the middle: no wobble, no worries.
steps: Fry the onion, potato, capsicum and zucchini until soft.
Whisk the eggs with a splash of milk and the cheese, then pour it over the veg.
Cook it gently, then finish it under the grill until the centre is set firm with no wobble left.
Serve it hot, and reheat any leftovers once until they are steaming.

meals.name: Big Brekky, Home Edition
meals.punLine: The full cafe brekky at your place, with firm yolks, hot mushies and precisely zero hollandaise.
steps: Fry the bacon until it is crisp and serve it hot off the pan.
Cook the mushrooms and halved tomatoes in the same pan until they are soft and sizzling.
Fry the eggs, basting or flipping them until the yolks are firm all the way through.
Toast and butter the sourdough, bake the hash browns until golden, and skip the hollandaise entirely.

meals.name: Pav The Way
meals.punLine: The pav stays a national treasure: baked meringue is cooked egg, so dessert is sorted.
steps: Whip the egg whites and sugar to stiff, glossy peaks, then fold in the cornflour and vinegar.
Bake it low and slow until the outside is crisp and dry to the touch, then cool it in the oven.
Whip the cream and pile it on.
Wash and cut the fruit yourself rather than buying it pre-cut, then crown the pav and serve.

swaps.swap: Tub ice cream, or frozen-banana nice cream
Fresh cooked-filling rolls, made into a sushi night at home
Crisped hot prosciutto shards over pasta
Firm-yolk fried eggs, or a fat slice of fully set frittata
Canned salmon and cream cheese bagel
White bean dip, or shelf-stable jar pâté, kept in the fridge once opened
Decaf oat latte, which tastes like the real thing at 4pm
Sparkling water, lime and frozen berries in the good glass
White bean dip or beetroot dip, hold the feta
